Method. Photon transfer from 42 flat pairs in 6 sets: (μ_F − μ_offset)/(σ²_F − σ²_B), per colour plane, central 50 % of the frame; cross-checked by the slope of variance vs signal over tiles.

To improve: For a full photon transfer curve (saturation, linearity): flats at 8–20 exposure times from ~1 % to past saturation, with the same panel brightness and filter (two frames each).

Saturation capacity = (white level − offset) × gain: the ADC clip, which can be below the pixel's physical full well. DR = log₂(saturation / read noise).

Method. No bias frames, so the dark signal can't be separated from the offset. The temporal noise of Dark · 300 s · -5 °C · 28 subs bounds read noise and dark current together: RN² + D·t ≤ g²·σ²_dark.

To improve: Bias frames (or darks at a second, much shorter exposure) at this gain, offset and temperature.
To improve: Darks at three or more sensor temperatures (≥ 5 °C apart) give the doubling temperature.

Read noise is only an upper limit here (no bias frames), so the recommended sub lengths are upper limits too; with the published read noise (0.79 e⁻) they are shorter, as shown.

Method. Sky flux = (darkest frame's median − offset − dark signal) × gain / exposure; Glover's criterion t = R² / (P·((1+x)² − 1)).

Data checks

Calibration coverage — Light · Ha · 300 s · -5 °C · 5 subs: missing bias (or dark flats) for the flats
Calibration coverage — Light · OIII · 300 s · -5 °C · 5 subs: missing bias (or dark flats) for the flats
Calibration coverage — Light · R · 5 s · -5 °C · 5 subs: missing darks at 5 s, bias (or dark flats) for the flats
Number format — 12-bit data stored ×16
Values are multiples of 16: a 12-bit ADC stored as 16-bit. 1 native ADU = 16 file ADU; quantisation noise is 16/√12 = 4.6 file ADU rms.
Offset clipping — No pixels clipped at zero
When the offset is too low, the noise distribution of bias and darks is cut at zero: read noise and dark current are underestimated and faint signal is lost. Raise the offset until no pixels sit at 0.
In-camera filtering — Pixel noise independent (|ρ| ≤ 0.001)
Read and shot noise are independent from pixel to pixel, so the difference of two frames should show no correlation between neighbouring same-colour pixels. Correlation means the camera filtered or compressed the raw data (e.g. Sony's 'star eater' on long exposures), which lowers the measured variance and inflates the gain.
